input.question: How can there be a maximum speed if there is no absolute frame of reference in space?
input.ground_truth: > I could travel at a constant speed, choose myself as the frame of reference and claim that I'm standing still. Now, suppose I first accelerate to the speed of 0.99c, then establish my current fixed speed as the speed 0. Wouldn't I then be able to continue to accelerate, eventually past c? Yes. You can. The difference however is that, in relation to an observer "standing still", time is passing slower for you, your length is contracted etc. So, in relation to this observer you won't be able to reach *c*. However, in your perspective, you really will be able to reach your destination faster if you keep accelerating as if relativity didn't exist. The thing is that you will reach your destination faster because as you accelerate, time slows down for you, so in a blink of an eye, you're in the other side of the universe (depending on how much you accelerated from 0.99c)

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How can there be a maximum speed if there is no absolute frame of reference in space?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend are both on skateboards, and you're both rolling really fast in different directions. Now, if you look at your friend from your skateboard, it might look like your friend is moving a little bit slower than if someone standing on the ground (like your mom) looks at you both.

Now, imagine there's a special speed limit—like the fastest you can ever go, no matter what, is like a super-fast car's top speed. This is kind of like the speed of light in space! Scientists call this speed the "speed limit of the universe."

But you might wonder, "If there's no special spot in space that says 'this is still' (no absolute frame of reference), how do we know what this fastest speed is?" 

Well, think about it like this: even if you and your friend can't agree on who is moving or who is standing still, you both will always agree that nothing can go faster than that super-fast car's top speed. That's the rule everyone follows, no matter where you are or how you're moving. That's why we have a maximum speed in the universe, even if there's no "special" place to measure it from!
